bib.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

question: Can a pairwise sigmoid loss replace the batch-softmax contrastive loss in language-image pre-training, and how does it change the effect of batch size and training cost?
hypothesis: A per-pair binary sigmoid loss, which needs no global normalisation, is simpler, more memory efficient and better at small batch sizes than softmax (implied).
contributions: Pairwise sigmoid loss for language-image pre-training (SigLIP, and SigLiT with locked image tower)
Batch-size study from 512 to 1M showing saturation near 32k
Ablations on bias term, negative ratio, beta2 stability, label-noise robustness
Released SigLIP / mSigLIP models in big_vision

method.summary: Replaces the softmax InfoNCE loss with an independent binary sigmoid loss over all image-text pairs in a batch, with learnable temperature t'=log10 and bias b=-10 initialisation, computed in device-local chunks. Applied to LiT-style locked-image training (SigLiT) and from-scratch/unlocked training (SigLIP, mSigLIP) on WebLI, evaluated by zero-shot ImageNet and retrieval.
method.task: contrastive language-image pre-training (zero-shot classification and retrieval)

datasets.name: LiT image-text dataset
datasets.preprocessing: Images precomputed ViT-g embeddings, resize to fixed 288x288 only

datasets.name: WebLI
datasets.split: English-only subset for SigLIP; all 100 languages for mSigLIP
datasets.preprocessing: 224x224 images, 32k sentencepiece (C4 English), max 16 text tokens; scale-up runs use 256 patches and 64 text tokens

models.name: SigLiT
models.architecture: locked ViT-g (or AugReg B/8, g/14) image tower with precomputed embeddings; Base text transformer (Large 12-layer in 4-chip runs)
models.init_from: public pre-trained image checkpoints (frozen); text from scratch

models.name: SigLIP B/16
models.architecture: ViT-B/16 image + B text transformer, from scratch
models.init_from: random, or AugReg B/16 with 0.1 LR multiplier for unlocked fine-tuning

models.name: mSigLIP
models.architecture: B-sized ViT and text model, multilingual

other.bottleneck_token_embedding: K=96 with W=768, about half a percent ImageNet drop vs full 250k

models.name: CLIP (WebLI)
models.architecture: same as SigLIP with softmax loss

training.objective: sigmoid pairwise binary loss, -1/|B| sum_i sum_j log(1/(1+exp(z_ij(-t x_i.y_j + b)))), z=1 for matches else -1; t=exp(t'), t' init log 10, b init -10
training.optimizer: ScalingViT-Adafactor (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95) default; AdamW tested; LION for 4-chip SigLiT
training.lr: 0.001 default (peak 1e-4 for LION 4-chip run); 0.1x multiplier on pre-trained image tower
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then cosine decay to zero
training.warmup: 200M examples seen (SigLiT sweep); 6.5k steps (LION run); 10% of steps (label-noise runs)
training.tokens: examples seen: 450M to 18B (SigLiT), 3B/9B (SigLIP), 30B (mSigLIP), 40B (scale-up) plus 5B at target resolution
training.weight_decay: 0.0001 default; 1e-7 decoupled for LION run; none on pre-trained image weights when fine-tuning
training.hardware: Google Cloud TPU v4 (4, 16, 32 chips in small-budget runs)
training.compute: SigLiT B/8: 4 TPUv4 chips, 1 day; g/14: 4 chips, 2 days; SigLIP B/16 unlocked: 16 chips, 3 days; from scratch 32 chips, 2 days (72.1) / 5 days (73.4)
training.seeds: five repeated runs at 32k batch, 3B examples (Table 7)

other.resolution_scale_up: extra 5B examples at target resolution with 100x smaller LR and no weight decay
other.label_noise_runs: M/16 image + M text, batch 16384, 3.6B examples, peak LR 0.001

inference.samples: zero-shot; Table 7 reports mean and std of five training runs

metrics.name: XM3600 recall@1
metrics.definition: image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval averaged over 36 languages

eval.protocol: Single runs except Table 7 (five runs). Sigmoid vs softmax compared at matched examples seen across batch sizes.

evidence.quote: We use 0.001 learning rate with a linear warmup schedule for the first 200 M examples seen

results.claim: SigLiT with a frozen g/14 image tower reaches 84.5% ImageNet zero-shot on four TPUv4 chips in two days.
results.setup: Frozen ViT-g/14, Large text tower, batch 20k, 107k steps, LiT dataset, 4 TPUv4 chips
results.quote: This further pushes the 0-shot ImageNet classification accuracy up to 84.5%.

results.claim: SigLiT with a public B/8 image checkpoint reaches 79.7% in under one day on four chips.
results.setup: AugReg B/8 locked, 12-layer Large text, LION, batch 32k, 65k steps, 4 TPUv4
results.note: Table 1 prints 79.8 for this row, text prints 79.7

results.claim: Sigmoid loss beats softmax clearly below about 16k batch, and the gap closes at larger batch sizes (SigLiT, 18B seen: 83.6 vs 83.1 at 8k).
results.setup: SigLiT, ViT-g precomputed, B text, 18B examples seen, batch 8k
results.table: Table 8, row 8 k, columns 18 B sigmoid and softmax (83.6, 83.1)

results.claim: Batch-size gains saturate near 32k; a SigLiT trained at 1M batch gets 84.7 against 84.6 at 32k.
results.setup: SigLiT, 18B examples seen, sigmoid; batch 1024k vs 32k
results.table: Table 8, rows 1024 k and 32 k, column 18 B sigmoid
results.note: Text says the model peaks at 256k batch

results.claim: From-scratch SigLIP B/16 reaches 73.4% zero-shot with 32 TPUv4 chips in 5 days (72.1% in 2 days).
results.setup: B/16 + B text, WebLI English, batch 32k, 32 TPUv4 chips
results.quote: SigLIP’s more demanding from-scratch training reaches 73.4% zero-shot accuracy in 5 days with 32 TPUv4 chips.

results.claim: Unlocked fine-tuning of a pre-trained B/16 reaches 71% only when weight decay is disabled on the pre-trained image weights.
results.setup: AugReg B/16 init, 0.1 LR multiplier, 16 chips, batch 16k, 2.4B examples, 3 days
results.quote: SigLIP reaches 71% 0-shot accuracy on ImageNet, using 16k batch size, trained on 16 chips for three days.

results.claim: SigLIP SoViT-400M at 729 patches scores 83.2% ImageNet-1k zero-shot, above EVA-CLIP E (5B) at 82.0.
results.setup: Shape-optimised 400M ViT, 729 patches, 40B examples seen at batch 32k plus 5B at target res; baseline is EVA-CLIP E (5B), 256 patches
results.table: Table 3, row SigLIP SO (400M) 729, column Validation (83.2); baseline row EVA-CLIP E (5B) 256 (82.0)

results.claim: SigLIP B/16 at 196 patches beats OpenCLIP B on ImageNet zero-shot.
results.table: Table 3, row SigLIP B 196, column Validation (76.2); row OpenCLIP B 196 (70.2)

results.claim: mSigLIP B reaches 34.9% average XM3600 text-to-image recall@1 at 32k batch, beating the prior 28.5% from a 4B ViT-e LiT model.
results.setup: mSigLIP Base, 30B examples seen, batch 32k, 36 languages
results.quote: Our best result is 34.9%, which is more than 6% higher than the previously reported result 28.5%

results.claim: Scaled-up mSigLIP B gets 42.6% image-retrieval and 54.1% text-retrieval recall@1 on XM3600.
results.quote: achieves the state-of-the-art 42.6% image retrieval recall@1 and 54.1% text retrieval recall@1 for a Base model

results.claim: Beyond 32k batch, multilingual retrieval gets worse: average XM T->I falls from 34.9 to 32.7 at 240k while ImageNet stays flat (73.2 to 73.1).
results.setup: mSigLIP Base, 30B examples seen, batch 240k vs 32k
results.table: Table 2, column 240k, row XM avg (32.7); column 32k (34.9)

results.claim: Learnable bias initialised at -10 with t'=log 10 gives 63.0% vs 62.0% with no bias, and 0 bias with t'=log 1 collapses to 53.7%.
results.table: Table 4, row b=-10, t'=log 10, column INet-0 (63.0); row n/a (62.0)

results.claim: Sigmoid matches or edges softmax at 32k and 3B examples over five runs: 70.1 +/- 0.2 vs 69.9 +/- 0.1.
results.table: Table 7, row Sigmoid ViT-Adafactor (70.1 ± 0.2); row Softmax (69.9 ± 0.1)

results.claim: Lowering beta2 from 0.999 to 0.95 stabilises large-batch training, which otherwise spikes in gradient norm.
Keeping only the hardest negatives nearly preserves quality, random or easy masking hurts; class imbalance is not a major concern.
Sigmoid-trained models stay ahead of softmax under image, text and batch-alignment corruption.

limits: Large-scale WebLI is private, so the headline numbers cannot be rerun without it.
Hard-negative mining is flagged as promising but no efficient method is given.
Very large batches only help with a sufficiently long schedule; short schedules give too few update steps.
Noise-robustness figure is qualitative (read from Fig 7); no numeric table.
Comparison in Table 3 is to publicly released models with differing data and recipes; EVA-CLIP and CLIPA-v2 are concurrent.

code.snippet:
t = exp(t_prime)
zimg = l2_normalize(img_emb)
ztxt = l2_normalize(txt_emb)
logits = dot(zimg, ztxt.T) * t + b
labels = 2 * eye(n) - ones(n) # -1 with diagonal 1
l = -sum(log_sigmoid(labels * logits)) / n
